title: EnzymeRSI: A dual-loop recursive self-improvement system for enzyme design
abstract: arXiv:2611.06321v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Improvement in enzyme engineering is usually pursued by optimising which candidates to assay within a fixed model and workflow; when the bottleneck arises from a mismatched method or a failing workflow, that route is difficult to escape. We present EnzymeRSI, a dual-loop system for recursive self-improvement (RSI). The outer loop evolves harness assets without changing model weights, the inner loop develops prediction and selection algorithms under controlled conditions, and a cloud laboratory system is specified to close the physical loop with quality-controlled feedback. By updating its prediction strategy through iterative comparison, the outer loop raised the mean development-set Spearman correlation on ProteinGym by 0.044 across five assays, reaching 0.335 on CD19 and 0.683 on OPSD (rhodopsin); of the two first places, only CD19 was produced by the outer loop itself. tldr: EnzymeRSI提出了一种用于酶设计的双循环递归自我改进系统，通过外循环演进预测策略、内循环开发算法以及云实验室闭合物理反馈回路，在ProteinGym基准测试上显著提升了蛋白质适应度预测性能。
en_tdlr: EnzymeRSI presents a dual-loop recursive self-improvement system for enzyme design, where an outer loop evolves prediction strategies, an inner loop develops algorithms under controlled conditions, and a cloud laboratory closes the physical loop, achieving notable gains in protein fitness prediction on ProteinGym benchmarks.
